headline: Google says its planned giant data center in Visakhapatnam, India, will be cooled by air rather than water after residents raised fears about water shortages.
score_reason: Kept at 6: a large investment and a clear change of plan, but it is Google's own account and activists still want a pause.
importance_line: Residents of a water-short city get a promise that the site will not rely on local water, and other builders may face the same demand, but it is Google's own account, activists still want a pause and no power figures are given.
summary: AFP reports, as carried by Kuwait Times, that Google's Alexander Smith says a water assessment "pointed to pressure on the local watershed", so the company chose air cooling for its gigawatt-scale AI data center in Visakhapatnam, part of a 15 billion dollar investment due to open in 2028. New since The Hindu's 9 Oct report of protests across India over data centers' water, power and environmental effects, Google also says it pays the full cost of grid upgrades, while activists in Andhra Pradesh still demand a pause on new data centers.
notes: Source credited to AFP (the text ends '— AFP'); read at Kuwait Times.
